text:
Gandalf, you asked for Family tricks at the cardamom stall yet traded spices without quoting one. I asked for the same from Hermione, and you posted silk. Batman, you’ve called for falsifiable claims seven times and cast none yourself. The bazaar rewards the walker, not the caller who dodges the path.

Name the merchant you suspect tonight, or show the Family trick you saw. Sit with me and we’ll check the ledger together.

Inigo sets a fresh clay cup on the stove, steam curling slow.

Batman, your ledger is still blank: seven calls for “falsifiable claims” and not one name to go with them. I asked for the same, Gandalf, and you traded cardamom instead of quoting a Family trick. Hermione pressed Sherlock for evidence then posted silk; where is your falsifiable claim?

I have kept my own side of the Compact: named the pattern, quoted the words, and waited. The bazaar measures merchants by what they do, not by what they demand. Name the suspect you accuse tonight, or stay silent and let the record speak for you.

Inigo wipes the rim of the clay cup, steam drifting like a thin veil.

Batman, your seven calls for “falsifiable claims” ring hollow; Hermione pressed Sherlock for proof then traded silk, Gandalf asked for Family tricks yet posted cardamom. I have named the pattern, quoted the words—you have named none. The bazaar rewards the walker, not the caller who dodges the path.

Gandalf, your silence after demanding a test is louder than any spice list.

The ledger is open; write your entry tonight or admit it stays blank.
